source_text: Deus autem postea cum uideret orbem terrae malitia et sceleribus obpletum, statuit humanum genus diluuio perdere. sed tamen ad multitudinem reparandam delegit unum, quod corruptis omnibus singulare iustitia supererat exemplum. hic cum sescentorum esset annorum, fabrica-uit arcam, sicut ei praeceperat deus, in qua ipse cum coniuge ac tribus filiis totidemque nuribus reseruatus est, cum aqua uniuersos montes altissimos operuisset. deinde orbe siccato exsecratus iniustitiam prioris saeculi deus, ne rursus longitudo uitae causa esset excogitandorum malorum, paulatim per singulas progenies deminuit hominis aetatem atque in centum et uiginti annis metam conlocauit, quam transgredi non liceret. ille uero cum egressus esset ex arca, sicuti sanctae litterae docent, terram studiose coluit ac uineam sua manu seuit. unde arguuntur qui auctorem uini Liberum putant. ille enim non modo Liberum, sed etiam Saturnum atque Uranum multis antecessit aetatibus. qua ei uinea cum primum fructum cepisset, laetus factas bibit usque ad ebrietatem iacuitque nudus. quod cum uidisset unus ei filiis, cui nomen fuit Cham, non texit patris nuditatem, sed egressus etiam fratribus indicauit. at illi sumpto pallio intrauerunt auersis uultibus patremque texerunt. quae facta cum pater recognosset, abdicauit atque expulit filium. at ille profugus in eius terrae parte consedit quae nunc Arabia, nominatur, eaque terra de nomine eius Chanaan dicta est et posteri eius Chananaei. haec fuit prima gens quae deum ignoranit, quoniam princeps eius et conditor cultum dei a patre non accepit maledictus ab eo: itaque ignorantiam diuinitatis minoribus suis reliquit. ab hac gente proximi quique populi multitudine increscente fluxerunt. ipsius autem patris posteri Hebraei dicti: penes quos religio dei resedit. sed et ab his postea multiplicato in inmensum numero cum eos angustiae locorum suorum capere non possent, tum adulescentes uel missi a parentibus uel sua sponte, cum rerum penuria cogeret, profugi ad quaerendas sibi nouas sedes huc atque illuc dispersi omnes insulas et orbem totum repleuerunt et a stirpe sanctae radicis auulsi nouos sibi mores atque instituta pro arbitrio condiderunt. sed omnium primi qui Aegyptum occupauerant caelestia. suspicere atque adorare coeperunt. et quia neque domiciliis tegebantur propter aeris qualitatem nec ullis in ea regione nubibus subtexitur caelum, cursus siderum et effectus nota-uerunt, dum ea saepe uenerantes curiosius ac liberius intuentur. postea deinde portentificas animalium Sguras quas colerent commenti sunt quibusdam prodigiis inducti, quorum mox auctores aperiemus. ceteri autem qui per terram dispersi fuerant admirantes elementa mundi, caelum solem terram mare, sine ullis imaginibus ac templis uenerabantur et his sacrificia in aperto celebrabant, donec processu temporum potentissimis regibus templa et simulacra fecerunt eaque uictimis et odoribus colere instituerunt. sic aberrantes a notitia dei gentes esse coeperunt. errant igitur qui deorum cultus ab exordio rerum fuisse contendunt et priorem esse gentilitatem quam dei religionem, quam putant posterius inuentam, quia. fontem atque originem ueritatis ignorant. nunc ad principium mundi reuertamur.
thought_title: God's Judgment and the Early Descendants of Man
pass_a_gloss: But God afterwards, when He saw the earth filled with malice and crimes, decided to destroy the human race with a flood. However, to restore the multitude, He chose one, because among all the corrupted ones, a single example of justice remained. This one, when he was six hundred years old, built an ark, just as God had commanded him, in which he himself, with his wife and three sons and as many daughters-in-law, was preserved, when water had covered all the highest mountains. Then, when the earth was dry, God, having cursed the injustice of the previous age, so that the length of life would not again be the cause of devising evils, gradually diminished the age of man through individual generations and set a limit at one hundred and twenty years, which it was not permitted to exceed. But he, when he had gone out of the ark, as the Holy Scriptures teach, diligently cultivated the earth and planted a vineyard with his own hand. From which it is argued that those who consider Liber the author of wine are wrong. For he not only preceded Liber, but also Saturn and Uranus by many ages. When his vineyard had first produced fruit, he, rejoicing, drank and became drunk and lay naked. When one of his sons, whose name was Ham, saw this, he did not cover his father's nakedness, but went out and told his brothers. But they, taking a cloak, entered with their faces turned away and covered their father. When the father recognized what had been done, he disowned and expelled the son. But he, a fugitive, settled in that part of the earth which is now called Arabia, and that land was called Chanaan from his name, and his descendants were called Chananaei. This was the first nation that ignored God, because its leader and founder did not receive the worship of God from his father, but was cursed by him: thus, he left the ignorance of divinity to his younger ones. From this nation, the neighboring peoples flowed, as the multitude increased. However, the descendants of the father himself were called Hebrews: among whom the religion of God resided. But also from these, when their number had later increased immensely, and their own places could not hold them, then young men, either sent by their parents or on their own, when the scarcity of things compelled them, fled to seek new homes for themselves, and, dispersed here and there, filled all the islands and the whole world, and, torn away from the holy root, established new customs and institutions for themselves according to their will. But the first of all, who occupied Egypt, began to suspect and worship celestial things. And because they were not protected by homes due to the quality of the air, nor was the sky covered by any clouds in that region, they noted the courses of the stars and their effects, while frequently venerating them and gazing at them more curiously and freely. Afterwards, they invented portentous animals, which they worshiped, induced by certain prodigies, whose authors we will soon reveal. The others, however, who were dispersed throughout the land, admiring the elements of the world, the sky, the sun, the earth, the sea, worshiped them without any images or temples, and celebrated sacrifices to them in the open, until, as time passed, the most powerful kings built temples and statues, and established that they be worshiped with victims and incense. Thus, the nations began to stray from the knowledge of God. They are therefore wrong who contend that the worship of gods existed from the beginning of things and that gentility is prior to the religion of God, which they think was invented later, because they are ignorant of the source and origin of truth. Now we return to the beginning of the world.

bible_refs.note: story of Noah's ark and the flood

pass_b_english: When God saw that the earth was filled with malice and crimes, He decided to destroy the human race by a flood; yet, to restore the multitude, He chose one man, because among all the corrupted a single example of justice remained (Genesis 6:9-9:29).

This man, when he was six hundred years old, built an ark just as God had commanded him, and in it he himself was preserved together with his wife, his three sons, and their three wives, when the waters covered all the highest mountains (Genesis 6:9-9:29).

After the earth dried, God cursed the injustice of the former age, so that the length of life would not again become a cause for devising evils; He gradually diminished the human lifespan through successive generations and set a limit at one hundred and twenty years, which it was not permitted to exceed (Genesis 6:9-9:29).

When he had come out of the ark, as the Holy Scriptures teach, he diligently cultivated the ground and planted a vineyard with his own hand; when it first bore fruit, he rejoiced, drank to drunkenness, and lay naked (Genesis 6:9-9:29).

One of his sons, named Ham, saw his father's nakedness but did not cover it; instead he went out and told his brothers, while they, taking a cloak, entered with faces turned away and covered their father (Genesis 6:9-9:29).

When the father learned what had been done, he disowned and expelled that son; the fugitive settled in the part of the earth now called Arabia, and the land was named Canaan from his name, and his descendants were called Canaanites (Genesis 6:9-9:29).

This was the first nation that ignored God, because its leader and founder did not receive the worship of God from his father but was cursed by him, and so he bequeathed ignorance of the divine to his descendants; from this nation the neighboring peoples flowed forth as their multitude increased (Genesis 6:9-9:29).

The descendants of the father himself, however, were called Hebrews, among whom the religion of God resided; but when their number later grew immensely and their own lands could no longer contain them, young men — whether sent by their parents or acting on their own, driven by scarcity — fled to seek new homes, dispersed hither and thither, filled all the islands and the whole world, and, torn from the holy root, established new customs and institutions according to their own will (Genesis 6:9-9:29).

The first of all who occupied Egypt began to suspect and worship celestial things; because they were not sheltered by houses due to the climate, nor was the sky ever veiled by clouds in that region, they noted the courses of the stars and their effects while venerating them and gazing at them more curiously and freely (Genesis 6:9-9:29).

Afterwards they invented portentous animals to worship, led by certain prodigies, whose authors we shall soon reveal; the other peoples dispersed throughout the land, admiring the elements of the world — heaven, sun, earth, sea — worshiped them without any images or temples and celebrated sacrifices to them in the open, until, as time passed, the most powerful kings built temples and statues and instituted their worship with victims and incense (Genesis 6:9-9:29).

Thus the nations began to stray from the knowledge of God; therefore they are wrong who contend that the worship of gods existed from the beginning of things and that paganism is prior to the religion of God, which they think was invented later, because they are ignorant of the source and origin of truth; now we return to the beginning of the world (Genesis 6:9-9:29).

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Latin text. Pass A provides a continuous prose translation, while Pass B provides a segmented version with appropriate scripture citations (Genesis 6:9-9:29) for the narrative elements described in the Latin. All clauses, including the specific details about the vineyard, the sons of Noah, the descendants of Ham, and the origins of Egyptian star worship, are preserved in both versions.

source: 'Deus autem postea cum uideret orbem terrae malitia et sceleribus obpletum, statuit humanum genus diluuio perdere.', English: 'But God afterwards, when He saw the earth filled with malice and crimes, decided to destroy the human race with a flood.'
